instruction: With VLC, cut a 3-second clip from src.mp4 on the desktop starting at 00:01, then use GIMP to turn it into clip_001.gif as an animated GIF.

metadata.explanation: Task requires user to use VLC to capture a 3-second clip starting at 00:01 from src.mp4 and convert it to an animated GIF using GIMP. The evaluator checks: (1) file exists at the specified path, (2) file is a valid GIF format, (3) file size is at least 50KB (realistic for video-to-GIF conversion), (4) GIF has at least 15 frames (expected for 3-second video at 5-10 FPS), (5) duration is approximately 2-4 seconds. LIMITATION: This evaluator cannot verify that the content actually comes from src.mp4 or starts at the exact 00:01 timestamp - it only validates basic file properties and plausible duration/frame counts for a 3-second segment.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly extracts GIF file metadata including existence, format validation, dimensions, frame count, and total duration using PIL
Metric properly validates 3-second duration requirement by checking duration_ms is between 2000-4000ms (allowing reasonable tolerance)
Realistic thresholds: min_frames=15 is appropriate for 3-second video at 5+ FPS, min_file_size=50KB is reasonable for video-to-GIF conversion
Complete coverage of verifiable requirements: file existence, GIF format, duration, frame count, and file size are all validated
Partial credit scoring breakdown (25% + 25% + 20% + 20% + 10%) is well-structured and covers all verification aspects
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Known limitation (acknowledged in metadata): Cannot verify content source (whether it actually comes from src.mp4) - this requires video fingerprinting which is beyond file-based verification
Known limitation (acknowledged in metadata): Cannot verify exact start timestamp (00:01) - this would require frame-level video analysis of the original and extracted segment
